work_order.understanding: Issue #58 carries two non-blocking review findings out of PR #55 (for #51), both confined to packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts. (1) The regression test added by that PR, 'keeps the sql.js wasm fetch patched for each test, not just the first', asserts only `vi.isMockFunction(globalThis.fetch)`, which is satisfied by any fetch spy at all — including one installed but serving nothing. I reproduced this: replacing the new beforeEach's body (index.test.ts:31-33) with a bare `vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch')` that delegates to the real jsdom fetch leaves the whole web suite green at 16/16. (2) The beforeEach's explanatory comment (lines 23-30) describes the pre-fix state in the present indicative — 'from the second test on, global.fetch is the real jsdom fetch again' — which is false of the shipped file, because that same beforeEach now reinstalls the patch before every test. This is the same tense defect the teardown comment in the same PR was rewritten to remove. The code is right in both cases; only the assertion's strength and the comment's tense are wrong. This is test hygiene on an already-merged test, not a product behaviour change: no source file, no interface, no screen.
work_order.root_cause: The regression test pins a vitest internal (that globalThis.fetch is a mock function) rather than the behaviour it exists to protect (that globalThis.fetch is patchFetchForSqlJS's sql.js wasm patch, able to serve the wasm asset from baseURL). `vi.isMockFunction` cannot distinguish the real patch from a bare pass-through spy, so the test passes for the wrong reason. Separately, the beforeEach comment was carried over from the pre-fix state and its tense now asserts something the code four lines below guarantees against.
work_order.approach: Two edits to one test file, no other file touched. (1) Strengthen the regression test: keep the existing `vi.isMockFunction(globalThis.fetch)` check (it is cheap and localises the failure), make the test async, and add a functional assertion after it — `const res = await globalThis.fetch(`${baseURL}sql-wasm.wasm`); expect(res.status).toBe(200);`. That URL is exactly what initSqlJS's `locateFile: file => baseURL + file` (packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.ts:55) requests, so a 200 means the wasm patch is really installed and really serving, and any other spy either rejects or returns a non-200. (2) Put the beforeEach comment's defect description in the past tense so it reads as the reason the beforeEach exists rather than a claim about the file. Leave everything else alone: the test keeps its last-in-file position (load-bearing, per its own comment), the beforeEach keeps its body, and the 'Last on purpose' comment above the test stays as written — I re-measured its claim after the change and it still holds (see evidence).

triage.diagnosis: GitHub's GraphQL API was down when the plan gate checked the split criteria. check-split-criteria.mjs:24 reads the issue body with `gh issue view 58 --json body`, and the call came back HTTP 503 "No server is currently available to service your request" from api.github.com/graphql, which gh rethrows as a non-zero exit and .sdlc/bin/lib/actions.js:103 rejects on. Nothing in this repository is wrong: the planner itself finished successfully (num_turns 37, subtype success, is_error false), wrote an 18957-character work-order.json, and the very next step validated it as `valid`. The step that went red is a bookkeeping read of the issue body, three minutes after it started, and nothing it read was wrong — the service was unavailable. That is an outage outside the repository, so the stage parks and runs again on its own rather than being retried immediately against the same endpoint. It is worth naming what this costs: the plan did NOT survive. In sdlc-plan.yml the split-criteria check (line 1010) runs BEFORE "Keep the validated plan" (line 1025), deliberately, so a refused plan is never stashed — and the ledger confirms the consequence: state/58.json on sdlc-state has work_order, validated_work_order and approved_work_order all null. The plan exists only as the plan-output artifact of run 37155921289 (ID 11285477541), and nothing in .sdlc/bin reads a previous run's artifacts — plan-strategy.mjs restores a plan only from ledger.validated_work_order or ledger.approved_work_order. So there is nothing for `resume` to resume, and the next run will spend a fresh planner pass. That is a cost of this outage, not a second defect, and not a reason to escalate a transient one.
